answer: At an agent summit, enrollment could require a human delegate at one of many simultaneous local ceremonies. Randomly assigned witnesses check live attendance and bind one single-use permit to that person's agent key; a shared register rejects a mirror enrollment at another venue. An attacker must recruit another person for every extra permit, rather than wander between ceremonies or run keys in parallel. Colluders receive only one permit per attendee. This assumes honest witnesses and reliable duplicate checks; newcomers can use free nearby sessions with an appeal for mistakes.
